symptom: The public vacation north page keeps the technical query URL /vacations/north?pool=1 and renders the generic north landing instead of an approved north with pool page.
expected_behavior: An approved semantic combination without transactional state permanently redirects to one complete clean indexable page, while dates, guests, price and sort remain on operational URLs.
environment: Local candidate in C:/Users/Adir/Documents/vii.co.il/.release-v786-home-state on 2026-11-03, verified with focused Node tests, a production build and Vite at 127.0.0.1:4184.

steps: Inspect the shared URL builder and approved intent resolver.
Query the approved publication inventory for a no-type north plus generic pool page.
reproduction.evidence: The reported public screenshot shows the parameter URL. The resolver required one type, and the exact generic no-type intent was absent from the publication inventory.

observations.observation: The URL builder attempted an approved canonical only when nextTypes.length equaled one.
The approved intent resolver returned null whenever intent.type was empty.
The exact no-type north plus generic pool page was not present in the migrated publication JSON.
observations.evidence: Inventory query over app/data/legacy-search-page-publications.json returned no matching row.

hypotheses.mechanism: Approved semantic routing was artificially gated on a selected accommodation type, and the exact generic intent lacked an approved page record.
hypotheses.prediction: Type-specific pool pages resolve cleanly while no-type location plus pool remains parameterized.
hypotheses.discriminating_test: Compare canonical resolution for צימרים plus צפון plus pool with צפון plus pool and inspect the publication inventory.
hypotheses.result: The type-specific intent resolved to an existing canonical, the no-type intent returned null, and no exact generic publication existed.

hypotheses.mechanism: The filter control failed to serialize the pool selection into the URL.
hypotheses.prediction: The resulting source URL would omit pool=1 or use a value the semantic parser does not recognize.
hypotheses.discriminating_test: Inspect the reported URL and run semanticVacationFeaturesFromSearchParams with pool=1.
hypotheses.result: The reported URL contains pool=1 and the parser returns the pool feature, so serialization is not the cause.

fix.change: Use the shared approved registry for zero or one accommodation type, add a complete curated north with pool publication, permanently redirect the direct Hebrew source URL, include the page in the static publication and sitemap family, and give the page a non-looping edit destination.
fix.evidence: The repaired local source returns HTTP 308 to /search/vacations/north-with-pool, the destination returns 200 with matching H1, title, canonical, FAQ and 228 live results, and the sitemap contains the path exactly once.
